differences.justification: The io.swagger.annotations.* annotations are purely descriptive. A change to one of them is equivalent to a javadoc update and is not an API change.
@JsonPropertyOrder only affects the order of the fields in the serialized JSON, which is not part of the API contract.
A model type used in a jersey3-client-v4 signature is defined in models-v4. Its changes are tracked in the models-v4 report.

The order of the constants of a generated enum shifts whenever a value is inserted alphabetically. It only matters to code relying on ordinal(), which no client should do against a generated enum: the wire format uses the names.
The JSON_PROPERTY_* constants are a generation detail of the model classes, not part of the API a client uses.
The model interfaces exist only to type the polymorphic model classes generated next to them. They are not meant to be implemented outside the generated code, so adding a method to one breaks nobody.
A changed parameter type means the call no longer compiles.
A deprecated element is announced for removal, which is what a caller planning an upgrade needs to see.
